docs.title: Picker Content Boundary: Query Dimensions + Write Schema
Portal and content service boundary
docs.text: From: Portal Plugin Factory team To: Content Management team Status: Draft — supersedes previous "operation contract" proposal Context: Content extraction and picker contracts

docs.title: 1. Background
docs.text:
The self-service plugin contains seven scaffolder field pickers. As part of the planned content extraction, these are split by data ownership:

  • Pickers that query Ansible content (collections, EE images) — the content boundary defined in this document. The Content Management team owns the data; we own the picker widget.
  • Pickers that query AAP resources (organizations, inventories, projects) — continue to use existing AAP API routes. Not part of this contract.
  • Pickers that are pure user-input (tags, pip package names, file names, MCP servers, SCM choices) — free text or template-enum. No content boundary. Not part of this contract.

What we are agreeing on here:

  • The query dimensions each picker needs (what fields are queryable on each content type)
  • The write schema (what the template form persists after a picker selection)
  • The authz requirement per query
  • The sourceId stability invariant (non-negotiable — stored values must survive upgrades)

What we are NOT prescribing: how the query is implemented. Whether sources and versions arrive as facets on a search query, relations, or a separate index is the Content Management team's decision. The picker is a widget; we do not own the query engine.

docs.title: The two pickers in scope
docs.text: Picker component Content it queries CollectionsPickerExtension Ansible collections from PAH / Galaxy / OCI BaseImagePickerExtension Built EE images available as base images

docs.title: 2. Current Behaviour (What We Ship Today)
docs.text: Understanding the current implementation makes the required data surface explicit.

docs.title: 2.1 CollectionsPicker
docs.text:
The picker today calls scaffolderApi.autocomplete with three resource strings in a cascade: name → source → version. The user flow is:

  1. Type to search collection names → select one
  2. Select a source (PAH instance, Galaxy, OCI registry) where that collection is available
  3. Optionally select a version at that source (or leave blank for "latest")

The value stored in the template form is:

interface CollectionItem {
  name: string; // e.g. "community.general"
  source: string; // source ID — stored in the EE definition file
  version?: string; // version string, or null for "latest"
}

docs.title: 2.2 BaseImagePicker
docs.text:
Currently static — available base images are hardcoded as a JSON schema enum in the template YAML. No API call is made at runtime.

The planned integration requires this to become dynamic — fetching available base images from the content catalog so that new AAP releases appear automatically without template edits.

The value stored in the template form is:

interface EEBaseImageRef {
  imageRef: string; // fully qualified: "registry/image:tag"
  digest?: string; // sha256:... for reproducible pinning (preferred for production)
}

docs.title: 3. Content Boundary: Query Dimensions + Write Schema
3.1 Collection type
docs.text:
What the picker needs to query:

Dimension Description Notes name Full-text / prefix search on collection name (e.g. "community.general") Powers the first autocomplete sources For a selected collection: what sources carry it (PAH, Galaxy, OCI, etc.) A relation or facet — not a separate RPC. Sources are IDs + human labels versions For a selected collection + source: available versions May be live-fetched or indexed — freshness is the content service's concern, not ours

Write schema (what we store and what must stay stable):

interface CollectionItem {
  name: string; // fully qualified collection name — stable
  source: string; // opaque source ID — MUST survive PAH upgrades (see §4)
  version?: string; // version string, or null/omitted for "latest"
}

Authorization: ansible.collections.view (already declared in backstage-rhaap-common)

docs.title: 3.2 Execution environment image type
docs.text:
What the picker needs to query:

Dimension Description Notes usableAsBase Filter to images that can act as a base image in an EE definition Boolean facet — not all EEs are usable as base imageRef Fully qualified pull reference (registry/image:tag) Written into execution-environment.yml digest OCI digest (sha256:...) for reproducible pinning Optional but preferred for production definitions recommended Whether this is the RH-recommended base for new definitions UI renders a "Recommended" badge; at most one true

Write schema:

interface EEBaseImageRef {
  imageRef: string; // written directly into execution-environment.yml
  digest?: string; // sha256:... for reproducible pinning
}

Authorization: ansible.execution-environments.view (already declared)

docs.title: 4. Non-Negotiable: sourceId Stability
docs.text:
The source field in CollectionItem is stored inside execution-environment.yml files committed to source control. If the Content Management team changes the opaque ID for a source across PAH upgrades (e.g. during a re-registration), existing EE definitions silently reference a source that no longer exists.

We need one of:

  1. A stability guarantee: source IDs are immutable once assigned. Decommissioned sources get a tombstone (still resolvable, marked deprecated) rather than a deletion.
  2. A migration event: an observable signal we can subscribe to when a source ID changes, so we can update stored EE definitions proactively.

This is the single hardest dependency between our teams. Everything else in this document is a fresh build; this one touches committed customer files.

docs.title: 5. Open Questions
docs.text: # Question Impact Q1 Is Collection.providedBy in the current AutomationContentClient the stable source ID, or a display label? Determines whether we can use it as the stored source field. Write schema stability Q2 Is collection/version data served from a live PAH query or from a Backstage Search index (collator)? Determines picker latency, offline behaviour, and whether search is live-typed or request-on-open. UX + freshness model Q3 For usableAsBase — is this a computed field (introspection-derived) or manually curated? Affects whether new Red Hat EE releases appear automatically or require a catalog update. BaseImagePicker accuracy Q4 Is digest always available for catalog-indexed images, or only after a live registry fetch? Reproducibility guarantee

docs.title: 6. What We Commit To (Portal team)
docs.text:
Once the open questions above are answered:

  1. Implementing CollectionsPicker against the agreed query API — the cascade (name → source → version) maps to the declared query dimensions regardless of how the content service implements the underlying query.
  2. Implementing BaseImagePicker dynamic fetching against the usableAsBase filter.
  3. Publishing CollectionItem and EEBaseImageRef in portal-extension-common as the stable write schemas both teams import.
  4. Not coupling picker internals to RHDH APIs. The picker calls our abstraction layer; that layer calls the published content client. When RHDH changes the search seam, we update the adapter — not the picker widget and not the template authors.

docs.title: 7. Non-Content Pickers (Out of Scope for This Contract)
docs.text:
The remaining five pickers have no content ownership dependency:

Picker Data source Ownership after extraction EETagsPicker User-provided free text Stays in portal-scaffolder PackagesPicker User-provided free text (pip package names) Stays in portal-scaffolder MCPServersPicker Static schema enum from template YAML Stays in portal-scaffolder AAResourcePicker AAP API (organizations, inventories, projects) Stays in portal-scaffolder, continues to use AAP proxy ScmSelector Static enum (GitHub, GitLab) Stays in portal-scaffolder; may add Gitea if the content service supports it

The Content Management team is not blocked on any of these five. They are entirely portal-scaffolder owned and require no content boundary agreement.

docs.title: Current delivery scope
docs.text:
The Portal Plugin Factory provides the contracts and SDKs that let first-party and third-party plugins contribute to Automation Portal. This is an experimental implementation, not a claim that the full Content Experience Architecture has shipped.

Currently, native NFS composition and the agreed functional checks are complete. Content extraction and cross-team query/write contracts remain separate work. The upstream review branch is feat/portal-plugin-factory-sdk; anstrat-2497-poc retains the original development history in the fork.

Use Portal NFS composition for the current frontend integration contract. Earlier registry and Scalprum descriptions in historical architecture documents are not instructions for the native app.

docs.title: Internal developer-preview readiness
docs.text:
The internal developer-preview contract defines the proposed API boundary, supported launch subset, backend responsibilities, exclusions, and compatibility policy for consuming teams. Its implemented behavior is distinct from the policy awaiting joint agreement. Preview teams develop plugins in this repository's workspaces using workspace:^ SDK dependencies and the shared root lockfile. Native composition being complete does not mean team onboarding or all architecture requirements are complete; npm publication is not a preview requirement.

Before declaring a consumable preview:

  1. Agree on the documented API subset and breaking-change migration policy with SDK maintainers and consuming teams.
  2. Review the intended consumer's mutation and background-work paths. Migrate paths that bypass the agreed authorization/operation boundary, or explicitly exclude those features; frontend gates alone are not an exclusion mechanism.
  3. Complete the author guide's fresh-clone acceptance with the consuming team's workspace plugin: install dependencies from the root, build/test the required packages, export dynamically, and install the artifacts in RHDH. No external plugin repository or npm publication is required.
  4. Record the SDK revision, dependency versions, RHDH image digest, and tested artifacts. The current deployment baseline remains next-2.1 only.

Broader content extraction, additional launch combinations, and a standalone theme package are separate architecture work. They become preview prerequisites only if the agreed consumer use case requires them. Idempotency deduplication, automatic MCP exposure, and durable auditing are not current dispatcher guarantees; do not advertise them merely because metadata fields exist.

docs.title: Workspace ownership
docs.text:
The repository remains named ansible-backstage-plugins. Package ownership is organized under workspaces/, with one root Yarn workspace configuration and lockfile:

  • portal-core/packages/app and portal-core/packages/backend: development harnesses.
  • portal-core/plugins: shared Portal contracts, host, SDK, operations, and health.
  • self-service/plugins/portal-scaffolder: @ansible/portal-scaffolder, including templates, tasks, and the content pages awaiting extraction.
  • aap/plugins: AAP integration clients, authentication, catalog providers, user provisioning, and scaffolder actions.
  • apme/plugins: the third-party contribution example and its backend modules.

Root plugins/ and packages/ directories no longer contain application code. The WP-001 inventory tool and its inventory:scan script are maintained separately on the fork branch tools/wp-001, not in the SDK branch.

docs.title: Package responsibilities
docs.text:
All Portal packages below live under workspaces/portal-core/plugins/.

  • @ansible/portal-extension-common owns shared manifest, capability, launch, operation, entitlement, and content-type contracts. Runtime predicates belong on frontend descriptors, not in serialized contribution metadata.
  • @ansible/portal-extension-api provides frontend API references, clients, and native Blueprint/data-reference contracts through ./alpha. Its registry helpers remain available for legacy compatibility.
  • @ansible/portal-extension-host validates and filters native descriptors, renders eligible contributions, and supplies error boundaries, design-token wrappers, and an RJSF settings shell. Native adapters are exported through ./alpha.
  • @ansible/portal-core installs the portal frontend plugin's shared contribution, operation, and entitlement APIs. Its ./app-nav module adapts discovered pages into configuration-driven navigation.
  • @ansible/portal-plugin-sdk supplies reusable components, notifications, caching, context hooks, styles, icons, and theme utilities.
  • @ansible/portal-plugin-node supplies backend operation registration, identity/context helpers, audit emission, organization helpers, and health reporting infrastructure.
  • @ansible/portal-operations-backend exposes authorized operation dispatch and server-resolved organization/entitlement decisions.
  • @ansible/portal-health-backend exposes aggregated health at /api/portal-health/status. Backend health reporting does not imply that a health indicator is installed in the application UI.

A standalone portal-theme package is not present. Current shell integration uses Portal navigation, existing theme utilities, and an app-owned global-header wrapper. RHDH keeps its own platform header.

docs.title: Native contribution lifecycle
docs.text:
Plugins declare reusable host-owned Blueprint extensions in static ./alpha entry points. They supply content scope, host attachment regions, permissions, entitlements, and optional narrowing predicates.

The portal frontend plugin installs api:portal/contributions once. The provider collects native descriptors through NFS data references rather than a shared mutable module-load registry. The host validates ownership, contract versions, references, regions, and content scope before activation.

Content/source matching, enabled experiences, configuration, permissions, entitlements, and predicates gate component loading. Only eligible contributions are mounted, inside host error boundaries. Actions dispatch registered operations with the current subject; plugins do not supply handler URLs.

CapabilityLaunch is a discriminated union of slot, workflow, and operation launches, with optional operation follow-on behavior. Although legacy types still contain optional moduleName metadata, the native path does not resolve arbitrary module names imperatively. NFS declarations own component loading.

Host experiences remain content-quality-assessment, content-authoring, and content-migration. Portal scaffolder is a plugin, not a fourth experience. Built-in catalog overview content is not an APME Quality capability.

docs.title: Delivered functional slices
docs.text:
The current native implementation includes:

  • Collections, execution environment, repository, template, task history, and catalog-import routes, without duplicate /portal/* pages.
  • Entity tabs, overview cards, entity actions, catalog item actions, catalog tabs/columns, workflow launchers, and native scaffolder fields.
  • APME Quality, Quality activity, Dependencies, scan actions, Add repository, and manual registration/deregistration.
  • Configurable sidebar links/groups with plugin-owned route/icon metadata. Administration can contain RBAC or link directly to it; Settings is independent.
  • Native RBAC, Settings, Search, and source-app global-header integration, preserving authorization and existing logout behavior.
  • Catalog-removal reconciliation before redirect/refresh, without resubmitting an accepted removal operation.
  • APME-owned summary refresh while background operations remain active.
  • Trusted AAP direct/team memberships intersected with configured organizations, and server-side entitlement grants. Any granted membership enables a shared capability, subject to RBAC; multiple memberships do not select an active organization for organization-specific state.
  • Consistent organization context across operation and registration transports, central enforcement of declared operation entitlements, and authorized APME interactive workflow forwarding. Git repositories remain shared resources; new manual entries use default without AAP ownership annotations or catalog namespace mappings. Existing records are not rewritten.
  • Flag-controlled stable AAP user/group/template identities, aligned across authentication, catalog sync, and the extracted user provisioner. The frontend SDK reads trusted membership context from the backend rather than user namespace.

The legacy app is an explicit ?portalFrontend=legacy fallback. Do not install its side-effect registration entry point alongside native APME declarations.

docs.title: Verification boundaries
docs.text:
Packed dynamic exports were exercised on quay.io/rhdh-community/rhdh:next-2.1 using mock AAP authentication and a local APME gateway. Separately, the source NFS app was verified with real AAP login and completed scan-only operations with persisted findings and automatic refresh.

The named manual test-repository registration was created and removed through native surfaces, preserving the GitHub repository and existing APME history. These checks do not prove real-AAP authentication inside the RHDH container, successful scanning of every repository, or remediation/PR creation.

The closure regression run passed 30 targeted suites and 313 tests, with TypeScript and lint checks passing. This is a previous targeted result, not the current full-repository test count or a guarantee of GitHub CI status.

The current documentation passes the full strict build. Local documentation environments must install the configured theme and support Cairo shared-library discovery for social-card generation; a content-only diagnostic build is not equivalent to the full configured build.

docs.title: Content extraction and picker contracts
docs.text:
Collections, repository browsing, and built-image views still need their agreed content-owned boundary and migration. EE definition authoring and Portal picker widgets retain their appropriate authoring/scaffolder ownership.

The content boundary is a generic query with type-declared fields and a stable write schema, not a private RPC per dropdown. For collection and base-image selection, agree on:

  1. Query fields, source/version facets or relations, and freshness semantics.
  2. Persisted collection selections and image reference/digest schemas.
  3. Stable source IDs that survive upgrades and appear in EE definition files.
  4. Authorization on returned hits and the published client/transport boundary.

AAP-resource pickers remain AAP integration concerns. Free-text/template-enum fields do not block the content boundary. See the content picker contract proposal. It is still a proposal, not a jointly frozen production contract.

docs.title: Production contracts and delivery
docs.text:
Use the preview contract for the bounded internal authoring surface. Its proposed 0.1.x compatibility policy is not a jointly approved supported-release commitment.

Authorization migration remains for legacy mutation routes and automatic background scans. The current interactive checks do not create organization selection, gateway tenancy, or cancellation of already-running work.

Before broader release, agree on contract versioning, compatibility guarantees, and delivery ownership with the consuming teams. Package publication and out-of-tree onboarding are separate future delivery decisions, not prerequisites for this in-repository preview. Complete remaining architecture requirements independently of native UI composition; in particular, do not infer full multi-organization session support or durable audit storage from the current SDK helpers.

Repository renaming to automation-portal-plugins remains deferred pending coordination. The completed workspace move does not mean the repository rename or all planned architecture work is complete.

docs.title: Related documentation
docs.text:
• Portal NFS composition: native declarations, configuration, validation, and troubleshooting.
  • Content picker contract proposal: cross-team query and write-schema agreement.
  • Developer quickstart: explicitly labeled legacy compatibility example; use the NFS guide for native integration.
  • Design tokens: theme-adaptive styling.
  • RHDH dynamic plugins: deployment guidance.
  • workspaces/README.md in the repository: package ownership.

docs.title: Portal SDK architecture
docs.text:
The Portal SDK lets independently installed plugins contribute functionality to host-owned surfaces. Plugins declare capabilities and typed native frontend extensions; the host validates, filters, and renders them. Backend operations are registered separately so multiple UI surfaces can reuse the same handler.

This page describes the current implementation on the plugin-factory SDK branch. It is an experimental implementation, not a supported release or a claim that the complete Content Experience Architecture has shipped.

docs.title: Host, experience, and contributor
docs.text:
• Host: owns the supported interaction contracts, semantic attachment regions, context, validation, and presentation lifecycle.
  • Experience: a host-owned user goal such as Content Quality, Authoring, or Migration. A plugin is not an experience.
  • Contributor: supplies domain components, predicates, operation handlers, and plugin-owned persistence. APME is the current third-party example.
  • Capability: a plugin's functionality, with one or more entry points such as a summary card, detail tab, or scan action.

Self-service currently supplies the catalog and detail pages. It consumes host adapters without importing APME's implementation. Content browsing still awaits the planned content ownership split.

docs.title: Package and runtime relationships
docs.text:
Arrows indicate contract consumption or runtime communication, as labeled. This is not an exhaustive package dependency graph or plugin load order.

flowchart TB
  Common["portal-extension-common<br/>Manifests, capabilities, operations, subjects"]

  subgraph Frontend["Frontend"]
    API["portal-extension-api<br/>Blueprints, API refs, clients"]
    SDK["portal-plugin-sdk<br/>Reusable UI and utilities"]
    Guest["Contributor frontend<br/>Static alpha declarations and components"]
    Core["portal-core<br/>Installs shared frontend APIs"]
    Host["portal-extension-host<br/>Validation, filtering, rendering"]
    Pages["Host surfaces<br/>Self-service catalogs and detail pages"]
  end

  subgraph Backend["Backend"]
    Node["portal-plugin-node<br/>Operation, identity, audit, health infrastructure"]
    GuestBE["Contributor backend<br/>Domain handlers and persistence"]
    Operations["portal-operations-backend<br/>Authenticated operation transport"]
    Health["portal-health-backend<br/>Aggregated health endpoint"]
  end

  Common -->|"Contract types"| API
  Common -->|"Contract types"| Node
  API -->|"Authoring contracts"| Guest
  SDK -->|"Shared UI"| Guest
  Guest -->|"Static NFS descriptors"| Host
  Core -->|"Installs contribution provider"| Host
  Host -->|"Eligible contributions"| Pages
  API -->|"Operation client requests"| Operations
  Node -->|"Injected host services"| GuestBE
  GuestBE -->|"Registers operation handlers"| Operations
  GuestBE -->|"Reports through injected health service"| Health

portal-core installs api:portal/contributions and the operation and entitlement API factories. Its navigation module selects discovered pages using configuration. It is not a Module Federation singleton registry provider.

The frontend and backend SDK packages are libraries, not standalone page plugins. Contributor backends inject shared host services instead of creating independent operation or health registries.

docs.title: Native contribution lifecycle
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Declare["Plugin alpha entry point<br/>Blueprint and manifest references"]
  Discover["NFS discovery<br/>Typed descriptors"]
  Validate["Validate<br/>Ownership, versions, references, region, scope"]
  Filter["Filter<br/>Content/source, experience/config,<br/>permission, entitlement, predicate"]
  Load["Load eligible component"]
  Render["Render within host<br/>error boundary and loading lifecycle"]
  Omit["Omit contribution<br/>Diagnostics for invalid declarations"]

  Declare --> Discover --> Validate --> Filter --> Load --> Render
  Validate -->|"Invalid"| Omit
  Filter -->|"Not applicable or denied"| Omit

Entity/catalog descriptors reach the shared provider through stable NFS data reference IDs. Pages read its validated snapshot via portalContributionsApiRef. Scaffolder fields have a separate native input on the templates page; not every Blueprint uses the entity/catalog provider input.

Static declarations load with the plugin. Component loaders remain deferred until eligibility checks pass; a tab component loads when that eligible tab is selected. Runtime predicates narrow the declared scope and cannot broaden it.

There is no native module-load registration into a global mutable ContributionRegistry. The explicit legacy app retains separate compatibility helpers; do not install both registration paths in the native app.

docs.title: Operation execution
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
  participant User
  participant UI as Host action
  participant Client as Portal operations client
  participant Host as Operations backend
  participant Handler as Contributor handler

  User->>UI: Select Scan
  UI->>Client: execute(operationId, subject, input)
  Client->>Host: Authenticated request
  Host->>Host: Resolve caller and trusted organization memberships
  Host->>Host: Check operation permission
  Host->>Host: Validate input schema
  Host->>Host: Enforce declared entitlements for the operation scope
  Host->>Handler: Execute registered handler with context
  Handler->>Handler: Resource checks and domain work
  Handler-->>Host: Result or job reference
  Host->>Host: Validate output and emit audit event
  Host-->>UI: Response
  UI->>UI: Supported follow-on navigation and refresh

The client discovers the portal-operations backend and sends an operation ID, the current subject's entity reference, and optional input. The manifest does not supply a handler URL. A descriptor alone does not install a handler: the backend registers it through portalOperationsServiceRef.

The dispatcher independently resolves trusted memberships, rejects an inconsistent context, and checks operation permission, declared entitlements, and input/output schemas. The handler remains responsible for resource access and domain checks. An accepted scan request is not a completed scan; job progress and findings belong to the contributor.

REST dispatch, identity middleware, repository registration adapters, and APME interactive workflows use the same injected organization resolver. Identity namespace is not organization identity. APME scan operations declare requiredEntitlements: ['apme.scanning']; workflow submission, approval, and state/event routes also enforce entitlement and repository access before forwarding traffic or resolving SCM credentials. State/event reads do not require the scan mutation permission.

The AAP adapter verifies the authenticated AAP identity, resolves current direct organization and team memberships, and intersects them with configured Portal organizations. Entitlement grants control availability, not membership. For a shared repository operation, any granted membership enables the capability; operation and resource permissions must still pass. For example, a user in Engineering and Finance can scan a shared repository when Engineering grants scanning, even if Finance does not.

PortalContext.organizationId is present only when one organization is unambiguous; organizationIds carries multiple trusted memberships without selecting the first. Operation descriptors default to organization-specific scope and require one validated organization. Descriptors explicitly declaring organizationScope: 'shared', including APME repository operations, can execute with multiple memberships. Shared access does not select a partition for organization-specific plugin data.

Git repositories have no mandatory AAP organization owner. New manual entries use the default catalog namespace. The former portal.organization.catalogMappings policy and ansible.io/portal-organization ownership checks are removed; existing records and annotations are not rewritten. Catalog namespace and SCM owner are not substitutes for membership or resource authorization.

The frontend usePortalContext hook reads authenticated host context from GET /api/portal-operations/context; it does not derive organization from the user namespace or fall back to default. The backend independently rechecks authorization rather than trusting browser context.

Important: Frontend filtering does not authorize backend resources. Remaining legacy mutations, automatic scanning policy, and organization selection are separate work; these checks do not introduce gateway tenancy or revoke running jobs.

docs.title: Backend health reporting
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  Backend["Contributor backend"]
  Service["Injected portalHealthServiceRef"]
  Registry["Host health registry<br/>In-process state"]
  HTTP["portal-health-backend<br/>GET /api/portal-health/status"]

  Backend -->|"Push status"| Service --> Registry
  Registry -->|"Read snapshot"| HTTP

Health reporting is independent of contribution rendering. The endpoint aggregates plugin status; it is not a durable history store or a domain job tracker. A frontend health component exists in the host library, but the current deployment intentionally does not install a health dashboard or indicator.

docs.title: Ownership and compatibility boundaries
docs.text:
• RHDH loads exported plugin packages; Portal contracts define what their contributions mean. Platform adapters own discovery and authenticated fetch.
  • Plugins select supported semantic attachments, not CSS selectors or arbitrary runtime module URLs. Host pages own the layout.
  • Operations are separate from presentation. New server effects must use registered operations; remaining legacy mutation paths still need migration.
  • Common metadata must remain serializable. New native predicates belong on executable frontend descriptors, even though legacy contract fields remain.
  • The current manifest requires experienceId. The proposed advisory recommendation and richer host composition preview/activation/rollback model are not implemented by the generic attachments alone.

docs.title: Delivered scope and remaining work
docs.text:
The implementation has native tabs, overview cards, entity/catalog actions, catalog tabs and columns, scaffolder workflow launchers, and native scaffolder fields. APME demonstrates Quality, activity, dependencies, scan actions, repository registration/removal, and background-result refresh.

Do not infer universal launch support from the common launch union. Native entity actions support operations and constrained entity-tab follow-ons; catalog-header workflows use registered scaffolder template descriptors. Other combinations require a supported host adapter.

Remaining work includes content extraction and agreed query/write contracts, authorization migration for remaining legacy routes and automatic background work, remaining operation guarantees, configuration/default-off conformance, published preview artifacts, and repeatable release acceptance. Audit emission currently means structured events, not a durable audit database; idempotent metadata does not provide a persisted idempotency-key mechanism.

Packed dynamic exports were exercised on next-2.1 with mock AAP authentication. Real AAP login and completed scan-only work were verified separately in the source NFS app. These are bounded acceptance checks, not broad platform or remediation compatibility guarantees.
