docs.title: Portal SDK — Legacy Dynamic Plugin Deployment Notes
docs.text:
Historical compatibility notes: The singleton, Scalprum, Janus CLI and mount-point YAML examples below describe the earlier implementation. They are not instructions for the current native app or RHDH next-2.1 deployment. Native composition is now the default and does not use a shared mutable registry for contributions. Use the plugin author guide and NFS composition guide for current contracts. Use checked-in export-dynamic scripts and the local development runbook for current packaging; do not copy the legacy commands or compatibility table as supported-release guidance.

This guide covers how to export and deploy portal frontend and backend plugins as RHDH dynamic plugins, with specific attention to the singleton registry requirement.

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
RHDH loads plugins as separate JavaScript bundles at runtime using Scalprum. Each bundle is isolated — when two plugins both import @ansible/portal-extension-api, they would normally each get their own copy of the contributionRegistry singleton, making it impossible for host components to see contributions from community plugins.

The solution is to configure portal-extension-api (and other shared packages) as externals — RHDH serves a single shared copy that all plugins share at runtime.

docs.title: The singleton problem
docs.text:
Without shared packages:
  ┌─ host plugin ──────────────────────────┐
  │  portal-extension-api (copy A)         │
  │  contributionRegistry → (empty)        │
  └────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ┌─ community plugin ─────────────────────┐
  │  portal-extension-api (copy B)         │
  │  registerGitRepoDetailTab(...)         │
  │  contributionRegistry → (has tabs)     │ ← different object!
  └────────────────────────────────────────┘

With shared packages:
  ┌─ shared package ───────────────────────┐
  │  portal-extension-api (single copy)    │
  │  contributionRegistry → (has tabs)     │ ← same object
  └────────────────────────────────────────┘
         ↑ host plugin reads from here
         ↑ community plugin writes to here

docs.title: Export a frontend plugin as a dynamic plugin
1. Add the export-dynamic script
docs.text:
In your plugin's package.json:

{
  "scripts": {
    "export-dynamic": "janus-cli package export-dynamic-plugin --embed-as-dependencies"
  }
}

docs.title: 2. Create src/dynamic/index.ts
docs.text:
This is the entry point RHDH calls when the plugin loads:

// src/dynamic/index.ts
import {
  registerManifest,
  registerGitRepoDetailTab,
} from '@ansible/portal-extension-api';
import { myPluginManifest } from '../manifest';
import { TrustSignalsTab } from '../components/TrustSignalsTab';

registerManifest(myPluginManifest);

registerGitRepoDetailTab({
  id: 'my-plugin.trust-signals',
  label: 'Trust Signals',
  component: TrustSignalsTab,
});

Important: The dynamic/index.ts entry point is called once when RHDH loads the bundle. Keep it side-effect-only — register contributions, but do not fetch data or mount React trees here.

docs.title: 3. Configure shared packages
docs.text:
In your plugin's package.json, declare the portal SDK packages as peer dependencies (not bundled dependencies):

{
  "peerDependencies": {
    "react": "^18.3.0",
    "@backstage/core-plugin-api": "*",
    "@ansible/portal-extension-api": "workspace:^",
    "@ansible/portal-plugin-sdk": "workspace:^"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@ansible/portal-extension-api": "workspace:^",
    "@ansible/portal-plugin-sdk": "workspace:^"
  }
}

Peer dependencies are not bundled into the dynamic plugin output — they are loaded from the shared package store at runtime.

docs.title: 4. Configure in dynamic-plugins.yaml
docs.text:
In the RHDH configuration file that controls which dynamic plugins are loaded:

plugins:
  # Host plugin (always enabled — owns the shared packages)
  - package: '@ansible/plugin-backstage-self-service'
    disabled: false
    pluginConfig:
      dynamicPlugins:
        frontend:
          ansible.plugin-backstage-self-service:
            mountPoints:
              - mountPoint: 'entity.page.overview/cards'
                importName: 'EntitySwitch'

  # Community plugin
  - package: '@my-org/my-plugin'
    disabled: false
    pluginConfig:
      dynamicPlugins:
        frontend:
          my-org.my-plugin:
            # Dynamic entry point is called automatically on load
            dynamicRoutes: []

sharedPackages:
  # The portal SDK packages MUST be declared here as singletons.
  # This ensures all plugins share one registry instance.
  - package: '@ansible/portal-extension-api'
    singleton: true
  - package: '@ansible/portal-plugin-sdk'
    singleton: true
  - package: '@ansible/portal-extension-common'
    singleton: true

  # Standard Backstage shared packages (also required)
  - package: '@backstage/core-plugin-api'
    singleton: true
  - package: 'react'
    singleton: true
  - package: 'react-dom'
    singleton: true
  - package: '@material-ui/core'
    singleton: true

docs.title: Export a backend plugin as a dynamic plugin
docs.text: Backend plugins are deployed as Node.js modules. The export process is simpler because there is no singleton concern — Node.js require() caches modules by file path within a single process.

docs.title: 1. Add the export script
docs.text:
{
  "scripts": {
    "export-dynamic": "janus-cli package export-dynamic-plugin"
  }
}

docs.title: 2. Register the backend plugin
docs.text:
RHDH backend dynamic plugins are registered via the dynamic-plugins.yaml backend section:

plugins:
  - package: '@ansible/portal-health-backend'
    disabled: false

  - package: '@my-org/my-plugin-backend'
    disabled: false

docs.title: 3. Configure in app-config.yaml
docs.text:
Your backend plugin's configuration goes under its pluginId:

my-plugin:
  # Plugin-specific configuration
  syncIntervalMinutes: 30
  retryCount: 3

Access it in your plugin via coreServices.rootConfig.

docs.title: Build and publish
docs.text:
# Build the dynamic plugin export
yarn workspace @my-org/my-plugin export-dynamic

# The output is in dist-dynamic/
ls dist-dynamic/

# For RHDH, package it as an OCI image:
yarn workspace @my-org/my-plugin build-image \
  --tag quay.io/my-org/my-plugin:1.0.0

docs.title: Verify singleton wiring locally
docs.text:
To verify that the registry singleton is shared correctly in the local dev environment:

  1. Start the dev server: yarn start
  2. Open the browser console
  3. Look for DynamicExtensionDiscovery log messages — they appear on startup and list all registered manifests
  4. If a plugin registered a contribution but it doesn't appear in the UI, it's likely a singleton misconfiguration

In the dev environment (yarn start), all packages are loaded from the monorepo and the singleton works automatically — no special configuration is needed.

docs.title: "Contribution registered but not rendered"
docs.text: The plugin's registerGitRepoDetailTab call hit a different contributionRegistry instance than the host reads from. Fix: ensure @ansible/portal-extension-api is listed in sharedPackages with singleton: true.

docs.title: "Cannot find module 'ansible/portal-extension-api'"
docs.text: The package is listed as a peer dependency but is not in sharedPackages. Add it, or temporarily add it to dependencies (which bundles it — workaround only, breaks the singleton).

docs.title: "Manifest validation failed"
docs.text:
Check the browser console for [DynamicExtensionDiscovery] error messages. The most common causes:

  • capabilityId contains spaces or uppercase
  • experienceId references an ID not in EXPERIENCE_IDS
  • launch.type is misspelled

Run validateManifest in a test to catch these before deployment:

import { validateManifest } from '@ansible/portal-extension-host';

test('my manifest is valid', () => {
  const result = validateManifest(myPluginManifest);
  expect(result.valid).toBe(true);
  expect(result.errors).toHaveLength(0);
});

docs.title: Health status shows "UNKNOWN"
docs.text:
The backend plugin has not called pushHealthStatus. Check that:

  1. createPortalPlugin({ pluginId: '...' }) is called with the correct pluginId
  2. pushHealthStatus({ state: 'READY', ... }) is called in the registerInit callback after initialization
  3. @ansible/portal-health-backend is registered in packages/backend/src/index.ts

docs.title: Version compatibility
docs.text:
Portal SDK version Backstage version RHDH version 0.x (historical) ^1.39.1 2.0+

The SDK packages follow semantic versioning. Shared package declarations in dynamic-plugins.yaml should pin to a minor version to prevent breaking changes from automatically deployed updates.

docs.title: auth-backend-module-rhaap-provider
docs.text: The auth-backend-module-rhaap-provider is an authentication plugin for Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform (AAP) that enables OAuth2-based single sign-on (SSO) integration with Backstage.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This plugin provides external authentication capabilities using AAP's OAuth2 implementation, allowing users to authenticate with Backstage using their existing AAP credentials.

Note: This plugin handles authentication only. For complete AAP integration, you also need:

  • catalog-backend-module-rhaap for user/team synchronization
  • Proper RBAC configuration for access control

For comprehensive setup and configuration instructions, see the External Authentication Documentation.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Build plugin as a dynamic plugin. Then configure your RHDH to load tar.gz with the plugin.

docs.title: AAP, Create OAuth2 application
docs.text:
OAuth2 application needs to be created in the AAP. Required properties:

  • Organization: Default
  • Authorization grant type: Authorization code
  • Client type: confidential
  • Redirect URIs: "https://RHDH_IP_OR_DNS_NAME/api/auth/rhaap/handler/frame"

docs.title: RHDH,
docs.text:
Fragment for app-config.local.yaml:

enableExperimentalRedirectFlow: true
signInPage: rhaap
auth:
  environment: development
  providers:
    rhaap:
      host: { $AAP_URL }
      checkSSL: false
      clientId: { $AAP_OAUTH_CLIENT_ID }
      clientSecret: { $AAP_OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET }
      signIn:
        resolvers:
          - resolver: usernameMatchingUser

docs.title: Detailed Documentation
docs.text:
For comprehensive configuration, troubleshooting, and advanced usage, see:

  • External Authentication Documentation - Complete setup and configuration guide
  • Home Template Listing - Templates home page, user-job-templates API, and AAP session errors
  • Users, Teams, and Organizations Sync - User catalog synchronization
  • Job Template Execution - Executing AAP job templates with authenticated users

docs.title: ansible/backstage-apme-common
docs.text: Shared library for APME frontend and backend integrations. Source: workspaces/apme/plugins/backstage-apme-common.

docs.title: Shared contracts
docs.text:
Provides APME types, configuration helpers, client/service contracts, repository normalization, scan-target resolution, operation status, and severity utilities. The ./operations export declares repository registration/deregistration, quality scan operations, permissions, and the scanning entitlement.

Browser-only exports such as ./api and ./useApmeEnabled are separate entry points. Backend modules must not import frontend API hooks.

docs.title: Related packages
docs.text:
• APME frontend: native presentation contributions.
  • APME catalog module: operation handlers, routes, and providers.
  • APME scaffolder module: repository-registration action.

Use Portal contracts for operation transport and host contribution metadata; keep APME-specific assessment behavior in APME packages.

docs.title: ansible/plugin-backstage-apme
docs.text: Frontend contributor for Ansible content quality and modernization. Source: workspaces/apme/plugins/backstage-apme.

docs.title: Native contributions
docs.text:
The ./alpha entry point exports the apme frontend plugin with Quality, Quality activity, and Dependencies tabs; overview summaries; scan and deregistration actions; catalog tabs/columns; Add repository; and a repository URL scaffolder field.

The plugin contributes through Portal Blueprints rather than importing self-service page components. Components use the APME API factory registered through the native plugin.

docs.title: Availability and lifecycle
docs.text:
Scanning requires ansible.apme.enabled: true, the host-resolved apme.scanning entitlement, and applicable permissions. Configuration alone does not authorize an operation.

APME owns scan-summary refresh while a background operation is active. The native scan action and interactive Quality workflow have different lifecycles; completed submission is not proof that remediation or a PR occurred.

See NFS composition, APME catalog backend, and APME shared contracts.

docs.title: backstage-rhaap
docs.text:
The backstage-rhaap frontend plugin enables the Ansible sidebar option and provides access to the frontend plugin

Note: This plugin was created through the Backstage CLI

docs.title: Installation with the new frontend system
docs.text:
The native frontend plugin is the default export of @ansible/plugin-backstage-rhaap/alpha. It provides the page:ansible extension at /ansible, with Overview, My Items, Create, and Learn tabs. The existing package-root exports remain available for legacy applications.

This repository's source NFS app loads the plugin in the full development profile and shows an Ansible sidebar link. The core and scaffolder profiles omit it.

Add the package to your frontend app's dependencies and register the native plugin in the app's feature list:

import { createApp } from '@backstage/frontend-defaults';
import ansiblePlugin from '@ansible/plugin-backstage-rhaap/alpha';

const app = createApp({
  features: [ansiblePlugin],
});

export default app.createRoot();

Keep the host's existing catalog, scaffolder, search, authentication, and API features installed. The Ansible page reuses those services for catalog browsing and template launching. Installing this page does not install those host features.

The plugin declares its route and page title, so native applications do not need a legacy <Route> registration. Hosts with custom navigation can link to /ansible. The page path can also be configured through app.extensions:

app:
  extensions:
    - page:ansible:
        config:
          path: /ansible

docs.title: Dynamic installation in a native RHDH app
docs.text:
From the repository root, export the plugin using the repository's RHDH CLI:

yarn workspace @ansible/plugin-backstage-rhaap export-dynamic --clean

The generated dist-dynamic package includes the native module-federation feature declared in backstage.features. Install that package through the host's dynamic-plugin installer. Native hosts discover its /alpha feature without the legacy dynamicRoutes and appIcons configuration shown below. The current CLI also generates legacy Scalprum assets for existing deployments.

The legacy AppThemeFixer export remains available for hosts that use it. The native plugin leaves global theme styling to the host and does not register that legacy application listener.

git clone git@github.com:backstage/backstage.git
cd backstage
yarn install

yarn --cwd packages/backend add @ansible/plugin-backstage-rhaap

docs.title: ansible/backstage-rhaap-common
docs.text: Shared AAP integration library. Source: workspaces/aap/plugins/backstage-rhaap-common.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
Provides the AAP client/service contracts, SCM utilities, resource types, permissions, naming helpers, and user-provisioning service contracts.

Backend modules consume ansibleServiceRef to access the AAP service through dependency injection. Frontend consumers use browser-safe exports and the Portal/backend API seams rather than transporting AAP credentials directly.

docs.title: Related modules
docs.text:
• AAP catalog module: scheduled catalog synchronization.
  • AAP authentication: authentication provider.
  • User provisioning: on-demand catalog users.
  • AAP scaffolder module: resource creation and job launch actions.

For provider-specific connection configuration, use the related module's guide.

docs.title: ansible/backstage-plugin-catalog-backend-module-apme
docs.text: Catalog backend module for APME integration. Source: workspaces/apme/plugins/catalog-backend-module-apme.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Registers APME routes under /api/catalog/apme/*.
  • Provides the manual repository and learned-dependency entity providers.
  • Registers apme.repository.register, apme.repository.deregister, and apme.quality.scan operation handlers and permissions.
  • Registers the scanning entitlement, settings integration, and scheduled sync.
  • Pushes initialization and synchronization health through the Portal health service.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
backend.add(import('@ansible/backstage-plugin-catalog-backend-module-apme'));

Install the Portal root services and configure the APME gateway. A disabled APME configuration skips this module's registration; enablement does not bypass permissions or entitlements.

Deregistration removes the manual catalog registration or stops relevant Portal tracking. It does not delete the Git repository or APME project/history. See APME frontend and operations backend.

docs.title: ansible/backstage-plugin-catalog-backend-module-rhaap-user-provisioner
docs.text: Catalog backend module for on-demand provisioning of authenticated AAP users. Source: workspaces/aap/plugins/catalog-backend-module-rhaap-user-provisioner.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
The module attaches to the catalog plugin, registers a user entity provider, and connects its user-creation callback to userProvisionerRef. It consumes ansibleServiceRef and server configuration through dependency injection.

Provisioned users carry source-location annotations and group memberships. AAP superusers receive the AAP admin group membership used by the integration. Namespace handling depends on configured organizations; it must not be mistaken for the Portal host's active-organization entitlement resolver.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
backend.add(
  import(
    '@ansible/backstage-plugin-catalog-backend-module-rhaap-user-provisioner'
  ),
);

Install with the AAP shared library and AAP authentication module. User provisioning is separate from the periodic AAP catalog synchronization.

docs.title: catalog-backend-module-rhaap
docs.text: The catalog-backend-module-rhaap plugin synchronizes users, teams, organizations, and job templates from AAP into RHDH / Ansible Self-Service.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Build plugin as a dynamic plugin. Then configure your RHDH to load tar.gz with the plugin.

docs.title: AAP, Create token
docs.text:
Plugin needs access to AAP. Create a token as admin user:

  • AAP UI, top left corner, click username, User details
  • Select tab Tokens, click Create token
  • Required properties:
  • OAuth application: leave empty
  • Scope: read

Use token value as AAP_TOKEN

docs.title: RHDH
docs.text:
Fragment for app-config.local.yaml:

catalog:
  providers:
    rhaap:
      development:
        orgs: Default
        sync:
          # Sync users, teams, and organizations
          orgsUsersTeams:
            schedule:
              frequency: { minutes: 60 }
              timeout: { minutes: 15 }
          # Sync job templates (optional)
          jobTemplates:
            enabled: true
            schedule:
              frequency: { minutes: 60 }
              timeout: { minutes: 15 }
ansible:
  rhaap:
    baseUrl: { $AAP_URL }
    token: { $AAP_TOKEN }
    checkSSL: false

docs.title: Features
docs.text: This plugin provides the following synchronization capabilities:

docs.title: User, Team, and Organization Sync
docs.text:
• Synchronizes AAP users as Backstage User entities
  • Synchronizes AAP teams as Backstage Group entities
  • Synchronizes AAP organizations as Backstage Group entities
  • Creates dynamic aap-admins group for superusers
  • Maintains group membership relationships

For detailed configuration and usage of user, team, and organization synchronization, see the Users, Teams, and Organizations Documentation.

docs.title: Job Template Sync
docs.text:
• Synchronizes AAP job templates as executable Backstage Template entities
  • Supports job templates with surveys and dynamic form generation
  • Enables direct job execution from Backstage interface
  • Provides filtering by organization, labels, and survey status

For detailed configuration and usage of job template synchronization, see the Job Template Documentation.

docs.title: Superuser REST routes (manual sync)
docs.text:
The catalog backend module exposes HTTP routes on the catalog service (paths are relative to the catalog plugin base URL, for example /api/catalog in development). These superuser-only endpoints trigger on-demand sync from AAP:

Method Path Purpose GET /ansible/sync/from-aap/orgs_users_teams Sync organizations, users, and teams GET /ansible/sync/from-aap/job_templates Sync job templates into catalog templates GET /ansible/sync/status Query sync status (supports query parameters such as aap_entities, ansible_contents)

Migration: Older releases used paths under /aap/sync_*. Those were replaced by the /ansible/sync/from-aap/... routes above. Update any custom automation or bookmarks accordingly. See the project CHANGELOG for details.

docs.title: ansible/portal-core
docs.text: Frontend host plugin for native Portal contributions. Source: workspaces/portal-core/plugins/portal-core.

docs.title: Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Installs the portal plugin's contribution, operation, and entitlement APIs.
  • Opens a configured installed page at /, or Templates when no override is configured and that page is installed. Otherwise, displays a neutral host fallback without creating duplicate catalog/entity pages.
  • Provides configuration-driven navigation through the ./app-nav module.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
Install @ansible/portal-core/alpha in an NFS app. Install the @ansible/portal-core/app-nav module when using Portal navigation, disabling the stock sidebar's singleton attachment. Contributors declare their own native extensions; the host does not import them for registry side effects.

Navigation selects discovered page extensions using portal.navigation.items. Items may be direct links or expandable groups; selection does not grant access.

docs.title: Landing destination
docs.text:
No landing configuration is required. By default, / opens /self-service only when that page is mounted. Without it, Portal displays a welcome message directing users to available sidebar destinations or their administrator.

To select another installed page, configure its exact path:

portal:
  landingPage: /self-service/collections

The path is relative to the app base URL. Use an exact mounted NFS page path, not an arbitrary nested route, external URL, query string, or fragment. Missing, disabled, invalid, or self-referential destinations display the host fallback; an invalid explicit override does not silently open Templates. Destination permissions remain enforced by the destination page. Sidebar ordering does not select the landing page.

For setup, migration, and verification, see configuring the landing destination.

See NFS composition for configuration and the implementation guide for the package boundary.

docs.title: ansible/portal-extension-api
docs.text: Frontend web library for Portal contribution contracts, API references, and clients. Source: workspaces/portal-core/plugins/portal-extension-api. This library is imported by contributors; it is not a standalone page plugin.

docs.title: Native contribution contracts
docs.text:
Import Blueprints from @ansible/portal-extension-api/alpha to declare entity tabs, overview cards, entity/catalog actions, catalog tabs and columns, workflow launchers, and scaffolder fields.

Entity/catalog descriptors attach to the host's api:portal/contributions provider. Native components load only after host validation and applicability checks. Shared data references do not require a mutable singleton registry.

docs.title: Compatibility
docs.text:
The root entry point also contains registry helpers and hooks for the explicit legacy app. Do not call those helpers for native registration.

Use the NFS composition guide for the current integration contract, not the legacy quickstart.

docs.title: ansible/portal-extension-common
docs.text: Shared contract library for frontend and backend Portal packages. Source: workspaces/portal-core/plugins/portal-extension-common.

docs.title: Contracts
docs.text:
• Plugin manifests, capabilities, entry points, and operation descriptors.
  • Slot/workflow/operation launch unions and operation request/response shapes.
  • Settings and entitlement declarations.
  • Canonical content-type, experience, and compatibility extension-point IDs.

Host experiences include Content Quality, Content Authoring, and Content Migration. Portal scaffolder is a plugin, not an experience. Runtime predicates belong on frontend descriptors rather than serialized manifests.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
Import shared types without importing the React host or backend SDK:

import type { PluginManifest } from '@ansible/portal-extension-common';

See the implementation guide for package ownership and remaining contract work.

docs.title: ansible/portal-extension-host
docs.text: Frontend web library that validates and renders Portal contributions. Source: workspaces/portal-core/plugins/portal-extension-host.

docs.title: Native host adapters
docs.text:
The ./alpha entry point provides the contribution provider, entity tabs/actions, catalog adapters, and scaffolder-field host components. Pages consume the provider's app-scoped snapshot; this library does not install duplicate pages.

The host checks contract ownership, versions, content/source scope, experiences, configuration, permissions, entitlements, and narrowing predicates before loading components. Contributions are isolated by host error boundaries.

docs.title: Shared rendering utilities
docs.text:
The root entry point exposes design-token wrappers, an RJSF settings shell, and legacy registry renderers. A health display component is available, but installing the library does not place it in the Portal UI.

See NFS composition for native integration and design tokens for styling.

docs.title: ansible/portal-health-backend
docs.text: Backend plugin for aggregated Portal plugin health. Source: workspaces/portal-core/plugins/portal-health-backend.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
Register the backend plugin alongside the Portal root services:

backend.add(import('@ansible/portal-health-backend'));

The endpoint GET /api/portal-health/status returns a snapshot keyed by plugin ID. Backend plugins report through the health service supplied by @ansible/portal-plugin-node. States include READY, DEGRADED, UNAVAILABLE, and UNKNOWN.

docs.title: Verification
docs.text:
Look for portal-health: starting health aggregation endpoint at startup. Use the host's authenticated API access to inspect the status endpoint. A missing report is not proof that a backend is healthy.

The aggregator does not create a UI page or header indicator. See portal-plugin-node for backend SDK responsibilities.

docs.title: ansible/portal-operations-backend
docs.text: Backend plugin for authorized Portal operation dispatch and entitlement decisions. Source: workspaces/portal-core/plugins/portal-operations-backend.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
The ./alpha backend feature loader installs the host-owned operation, entitlement, and health services once, then loads the backend plugin:

backend.add(import('@ansible/portal-operations-backend/alpha'));

Contributor backends register operations through portalOperationsServiceRef. The host dispatches operation IDs with authenticated context and current subjects, not contributor-supplied handler URLs.

docs.title: Organization and entitlement policy
docs.text:
The AAP adapter verifies authenticated identity and resolves current direct organization and team memberships, restricted to configured Portal organizations. Entitlement grants under portal.entitlements.grants use the adapter's canonical lowercase organization names or '*'. A missing grant denies entitlement; a grant does not prove membership or replace RBAC. Existing AAP superuser access to configured organizations does not bypass grants or permissions.

The same injected resolver supplies operation contexts and entitlement decisions. The dispatcher rejects missing or inconsistent membership context and enforces every backend descriptor's requiredEntitlements before invoking its handler. APME scanning declares apme.scanning. Registration and deregistration remain available without that scanning entitlement, subject to their own permissions.

For a shared operation (organizationScope: 'shared'), any membership granted the required entitlement enables availability. A user in Engineering and Finance can use a shared capability granted only to Engineering, subject to operation and resource permissions. organizations: ['*'] covers the caller's configured memberships; it does not grant membership in other organizations.

Descriptors default to organizationScope: 'organization'. Those handlers need one validated organizationId, and organization-scoped entitlements must grant that organization. organizationIds can contain multiple memberships, but the dispatcher does not choose the first. There is no organization selector in this flow. Shared Git repository operations do not choose a storage tenant for organization-specific plugin state.

docs.title: Minimal AAP policy
docs.text:
With Engineering already configured in the AAP provider:

portal:
  entitlements:
    grants:
      - id: apme.scanning
        organizations: [engineering]

docs.title: Multi-organization AAP policy
docs.text:
Keep your existing AAP connection configuration and configure organization scope and grants as follows:

catalog:
  providers:
    rhaap:
      development:
        orgs: [Engineering, Finance]
        multiOrgEnabled: true
portal:
  entitlements:
    grants:
      - id: apme.scanning
        organizations: [engineering, finance]

With multiOrgEnabled: true, AAP user identities use user:default/aap-user-<id>; organization groups use ID-based names and namespaces. Authentication, scheduled catalog sync and the extracted user provisioner use the same naming contract. With the flag off, legacy usernames remain supported; the resolver performs an unambiguous AAP username lookup. A failed identity or membership lookup denies access rather than falling back to default or all organizations. Changing the identity flag changes affected catalog references; synchronize the catalog and sign in again after changing it.

docs.title: Generic host fallback
docs.text:
Hosts without the AAP adapter can use the generic configured resolver:

portal:
  organization:
    id: default
  entitlements:
    grants:
      - id: apme.scanning
        organizations: [default]

This is a trusted deployment context, not an AAP membership resolver. When the AAP adapter is installed, it uses the configured AAP organizations and verified memberships instead of portal.organization.id.

docs.title: Shared repository identity
docs.text:
Git repositories do not require an AAP organization owner. New manual entries use catalog namespace default; catalog namespace and SCM organization do not determine AAP memberships. Repository access still requires resource RBAC and the handler's repository type, URL/branch, provenance and tracking checks.

Remove obsolete portal.organization.catalogMappings configuration. The former mapping policy and ansible.io/portal-organization ownership checks are no longer used. Existing persisted entries and annotations are not renamed, backfilled or deleted by this change.

docs.title: Frontend context endpoint
docs.text: GET /api/portal-operations/context requires user authentication and returns userEntityRef, userId, and either one organizationId or multiple organizationIds. The frontend SDK normalizes these into a membership list for display. No active organization is selected for multiple memberships. Operation requests do not accept client-supplied organization context; the dispatcher independently resolves it.

docs.title: Interactive workflow boundaries
docs.text:
APME operation submission, approval, state/events, and remediation submission authorize trusted memberships, scanning entitlement, and catalog repository before forwarding gateway requests or resolving SCM credentials. Mutating requests additionally require the scan operation permission. Read-only state/event requests do not require that mutation permission.

This does not migrate every legacy settings route, change automatic scan policy, partition gateway storage, or revoke running jobs when a grant changes.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Operation denied although the action is visible: check backend descriptor requirements, registered entitlement definitions, grants for the caller's resolved memberships, operation permission, and the handler's resource checks.

User with several memberships cannot invoke an organization-specific operation: the handler requires one validated organization, not an arbitrary first member. Use shared scope only when the resource and operation are genuinely shared.

Shared repository denied: check verified AAP memberships, configured grants, operation and catalog read permissions, repository identity and tracking state. Do not add a namespace mapping or bypass resource authorization. Re-export affected dynamic consumers and restart the backend after changing contracts or policy configuration.

See NFS composition for frontend checks and portal-plugin-node for service contracts.

docs.title: ansible/portal-plugin-node
docs.text: Node library for Portal contributor backends. Source: workspaces/portal-core/plugins/portal-plugin-node.

docs.title: Backend infrastructure
docs.text:
• createPortalPlugin: scoped health and audit helpers.
  • portalOperationsServiceRef: shared operation registration and execution.
  • portalEntitlementsServiceRef and portalActiveOrganizationServiceRef: host entitlement and trusted organization-membership decisions.
  • portalHealthServiceRef: shared push-based health reporting.
  • Identity middleware, audit emission, and withOrganization helpers.
  • resolvePortalContext: authenticated user identity plus trusted memberships, independent of user namespace. organizationId is optional; multiple memberships are carried in organizationIds without choosing an active org.
  • resolveOrganizationMemberships: validates and normalizes the injected resolver's membership set. Existing single-organization resolvers remain supported through resolve; membership-aware adapters provide resolveAll.

docs.title: Operation and context requirements
docs.text:
Inject portalOperationsServiceRef instead of constructing a private dispatcher. Its service dependencies include the active-organization resolver and entitlement service. For isolated tests, new PortalOperations(logger, organizations, entitlements) requires both dependencies; there is no permissive fallback.

Backend operation descriptors declare requiredEntitlements separately from frontend presentation requirements. The dispatcher verifies organization context, operation permission, and every declared entitlement before running the handler. Handlers still own resource permissions, supported content checks, and domain authorization.

Descriptors default to organizationScope: 'organization' and require one validated organization before invocation. Use organizationScope: 'shared' for shared resources such as Git repositories: any granted membership enables the required capability, subject to RBAC. Do not use shared scope to choose a tenant for organization-specific persistence.

Identity middleware requires organizations, injected from portalActiveOrganizationServiceRef. The deprecated defaultOrgId option is ignored. If identity or organization resolution fails, the middleware clears portalContext; protected routes must reject a missing context.

docs.title: Usage boundaries
docs.text:
Inject host services into backend modules rather than creating independent registries in each dynamically loaded package. Presentation belongs to frontend contributions; registered operations can serve multiple UI surfaces.

The AAP adapter validates current direct/team memberships against configured organizations. The generic ConfiguredOrganizationResolver instead supplies a server-configured single organization for hosts without the AAP adapter. Neither adapter treats catalog namespace or SCM owner as membership. Shared repository access requires no AAP ownership annotation or catalog mapping.

Membership context is not an organization selector. Organization-specific handlers reject ambiguous multi-membership context rather than selecting the first membership. Audit emission does not imply a durable external audit store.

See operations backend, health backend, and the implementation guide.

docs.title: ansible/portal-plugin-sdk
docs.text: Shared frontend web library for Portal contributors. Source: workspaces/portal-core/plugins/portal-plugin-sdk.

docs.title: Reusable functionality
docs.text:
• Page headers, dialogs, empty states, links, and loading components.
  • Notification stack and synchronization polling utilities.
  • Pagination, cache, and subscription utilities.
  • Context/authorization hooks, icons, styles, and theme utilities.

The SDK is not a host page plugin and does not register native contributions. Use portal-extension-api for Blueprint declarations and portal-extension-host for host rendering.

docs.title: Styling and ownership
docs.text:
PageHeader renders a title, optional description/help tooltip, and optional consumer-supplied actions. It has no authentication or synchronization requirements. The consumer owns UI permission checks and action handlers, while backend authorization remains mandatory for protected operations.

Portal-scaffolder composes this layout through its local CatalogSyncHeader for catalog synchronization. The SDK's sync-aware PageHeaderSection and its props remain available as deprecated compatibility exports. Existing callers continue to work. New consumers should use PageHeader, and legacy callers should migrate before a separately coordinated removal. No removal version is scheduled.

EmptyStateView renders a title with optional description, decorative icon, and consumer-owned actions. It requires no catalog, authentication, configuration, or sync APIs. Plugins choose their own wording and control action visibility and handlers. Backend authorization remains independent of UI presentation.

Portal-scaffolder keeps collection-specific behavior in its local CollectionsEmptyState wrapper. Repository details uses EmptyStateView directly with repository-specific missing-data guidance. The SDK's older EmptyState and EmptyStateProps remain deprecated compatibility exports, without a scheduled removal. Migrate consumers before a separately coordinated removal.

Prefer shared components and theme-adaptive tokens over importing private RHDH UI implementation details. Synchronization/cache integration uses injected callbacks rather than direct imports of a content plugin.

docs.title: Authenticated context
docs.text:
usePortalContext() discovers portal-operations and reads its authenticated GET /context endpoint. It returns organizationIds, an optional organizationId, userEntityRef, loading, and error. A single unambiguous membership supplies organizationId; multiple memberships do not select one. Resolution failures leave an empty membership list, not a default fallback.

Use this context for display. Do not infer AAP membership from the user's catalog namespace or use browser-supplied organization values as backend authority. Registered operations receive only subject and input; the backend independently resolves memberships, grants and permissions.

See design tokens and the implementation guide for the remaining content-client and picker boundary.

docs.title: ansible/portal-rhdh
docs.text:
Optional native RHDH profile-menu adapter. Source: workspaces/portal-core/plugins/portal-rhdh.

The adapter consumes generic Portal profile contributions using RHDH's public GlobalHeaderMenuItemBlueprint. Only this package depends on the RHDH header. It has no AAP dependency and does not add a Create button or Create-contribution API.

Install its exported native dynamic artifact alongside the Portal contribution provider and RHDH global-header feature. To retain AAP Sign out while removing the stock Create shortcut, merge these entries into the existing configuration:

app:
  extensions:
    - gh-component:global-header/self-service-button: false
    - gh-menu-item:global-header/logout: false
    - app-profile-menu-item:app/aap-logout: true

The gh-menu-item:portal-rhdh/profile consumer is enabled by default. AAP Sign out requires the separate @ansible/aap-app-auth native module, backend provider, and public OAuth client/host configuration. Keep stock logout when the AAP contribution is not enabled. Preserve all other auth and navigation configuration.

See AAP logout configuration and the package README for prerequisites, export and verification steps.

docs.title: ansible/scaffolder-backend-module-apme
docs.text: Scaffolder backend module for APME repository registration. Source: workspaces/apme/plugins/scaffolder-backend-module-apme.

docs.title: Action contract
docs.text:
Registers ansible:register:git-repository. Inputs describe the SCM provider, repository owner/name/URL, and default branch. The action resolves the initiating user and executes the registered apme.repository.register operation.

The action delegates persistence and catalog ownership to the APME catalog module; it does not import self-service frontend components or live in the AAP scaffolder module. Legacy owner input is not treated as authorization.

docs.title: Integration
docs.text:
backend.add(import('@ansible/scaffolder-backend-module-apme'));

Install APME catalog backend and Portal operation services before using the action. The repository registration template lives under workspaces/apme/plugins/backstage-apme/templates/apme-register-git-repository/; it must also be registered as a catalog location.

See APME frontend for the native field and workflow launcher.

docs.title: scaffolder-backend-module-backstage-rhaap
docs.text:
The scaffolder-backend-module-backstage-rhaap plugin scaffolds an Ansible collection or playbook project and adds the repo to source control. The scaffolder is dependent on ansible-devtools-server.

Note: This plugin was created through the Backstage CLI

docs.title: Installation - with upstream backstage
docs.text: The plugin is tested with backstage version '1.27.7'

docs.title: Setup backstage
docs.text:
git clone git@github.com:backstage/backstage.git
cd backstage
yarn install

Note: This has neen tested with node version v18.19.0.

docs.title: Configure Backstage with the GitHub authentication
docs.text: Refer https://backstage.io/docs/auth/github/provider

docs.title: Add the package
docs.text:
# From your Backstage root directory
yarn --cwd packages/backend add @ansible/plugin-scaffolder-backend-module-backstage-rhaap

Or

cd plugins/scaffolder-backend-module-backstage-rhaap
yarn install
  1. Manually copy the plugins/scaffolder-backend-module-backstage-rhaap directory to the plugins folder in the backstage root directory.
  2. Update the packages/backend/package.json file in the backstage root directory to add the dependencies under the dependencies sections as follows:
     "@backstage/plugin-azure-sites-common": "workspace:^",
+    "@ansible/plugin-scaffolder-backend-module-backstage-rhaap": "^x.y.z",
     "@backstage/plugin-badges-backend": "workspace:^",

docs.title: Adding the plugin to the correct places to register the scaffolder plugin
docs.text:

+import { createAnsibleContentAction } from '@ansible/plugin-scaffolder-backend-module-backstage-rhaap';

docs.title: Add ansible-rhdh-templates reference in app-config.yaml
docs.text:
This loads the templates from the ansible-rhdh-templates repository in Templates.

diff --git a/app-config.yaml b/app-config.yaml
index cb701705411b..efca1acfd19b 100644
--- a/app-config.yaml
+++ b/app-config.yaml
@@ -200,7 +200,7 @@ allure:
 integrations:
   github:
     - host: github.com
@@ -305,6 +305,21 @@ catalog:
       target: ../../plugins/scaffolder-backend/sample-templates/all-templates.yaml
       rules:
         - allow: [Template]
+    - type: url
+      target: https://github.com/ansible/ansible-rhdh-templates/blob/main/all.yaml
+      rules:
+        - allow: [Template]

docs.title: Start scaffolder backend
docs.text:
Run the following commands from the root folder of the backstage.

Backend

yarn start-backend

Backend - VS Code debug

Enable > Auto Attach: With Flag

yarn start-backend --inspect

docs.text:

dynamicPlugins:

docs.title: Creator service configuration and DevSpaces configuration
docs.text:
Add the devSpaces and creatorService in the app-config.yaml file. The devSpaces baseUrl is optional. It adds the Ansible DevSpaces option to the Catalog UI.

ansible:
  devSpaces:
    baseUrl: 'https://devspaces.apps.ansible-rhdh.testing.ansible.com/'
  creatorService:
    baseUrl: '127.0.0.1'
    port: '8000'

catalog:
  stitchingStrategy:
    immediate: true
  orphanStrategy: delete
  processingInterval: { seconds: 10 }
  pollingInterval: { seconds: 1 }
  stitchTimeout: { minutes: 1 }
  import:
    entityFilename: catalog-info.yaml
    pullRequestBranchName: backstage-integration
  rules:
    - allow:
        [Component, System, Group, Resource, Location, Template, API, Users]
  locations:
    - type: url
      target: https://github.com/ansible/ansible-rhdh-templates/blob/main/all.yaml
      rules:
        - allow: [Template]
  providers:
    rhaap:
      dev:
        schedule:
          frequency: { minutes: 30 }
          timeout: { seconds: 5 }
ansible:
  rhaap:
    baseUrl: { $AAP_URL }
    checkSSL: false

docs.title: self-service
docs.text:
The self-service plugin is the frontend plugin for Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform. First page (catalog) is available at /self-service/catalog.

To be fully functional, it requires other plugins for Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform:

  • auth--backend-module-rhaap-provider
  • catalog-backend-module-rhaap
  • scaffolder-backend-module-backstage-rhaap

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text:
Your plugin has been added to the example app in this repository, meaning you'll be able to access it by running yarn start in the root directory, and then navigating to /self-service.

You can also serve the plugin in isolation by running yarn start in the plugin directory. This method of serving the plugin provides quicker iteration speed and a faster startup and hot reloads. It is only meant for local development, and the setup for it can be found inside the /dev directory.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Build plugin as a dynamic plugin. Then configure your Ansible Self-Service to load tar.gz with the plugin.

docs.title: RHDH
docs.text:
Fragment for app-config.local.yaml:

dynamicPlugins:
  frontend:
    ansible.plugin-backstage-self-service:
      dynamicRoutes:
        - importName: SelfServicePage
          path: /self-service/*

docs.title: Additional configuration for sidebar
docs.text:
Add this to your app-config-*.yaml:

app:
  branding:
    fullLogo: data:image/svg+xml;base64,

dynamicPlugins:
  frontend:
    default.main-menu-items:
      menuItems:
        default.mycatalog:
          title: Browse
          icon: home
          to: /self-service/catalog
          priority: 120
        default.myitem:
          title: My items
          icon: category
          to: /self-service/task/list
          priority: 110
        default.home:
          title: ''
          icon: home
          to: /
          priority: 100
        default.catalog:
          title: ''
          icon: category
          to: catalog
          priority: 80
        default.my-group:
          title: ''
          icon: group
          priority: 70
        default.apis:
          title: ''
          icon: extension
          to: api-docs
          priority: 60
        default.learning-path:
          title: ''
          icon: school
          to: learning-paths
          priority: 50
        default.create:
          title: ''
          icon: add
          to: create
          priority: 40
    internal.plugin-dynamic-plugins-info:
      appIcons:
        - name: pluginsInfoIcon
          importName: PluginsInfoIcon
        - name: adminIcon
          importName: AdminIcon
      dynamicRoutes:
        - path: /extensions
          importName: DynamicPluginsInfoPage
      menuItems:
        admin:
          title: 'Administration'
          icon: adminIcon
        plugins:
          parent: admin
          title: RBAC
          to: rbac
          icon: pluginsInfoIcon
        licensing:
          parent: admin
          title: ''
          to: licensing
          icon: pluginsInfoIcon
        extensions:
          parent: admin
          title: ''
          to: extensions
          icon: pluginsInfoIcon
